Update Git Graph from inside the app, switch repositories from the title bar, and see each repository's latest release in CI/CD.

### Updates, inside the app

- **Settings → About** has one button: **Check for updates**. If there is a newer version it turns into **Update to x.y.z**; if you already have the latest it says **Already up to date**.
- When Git Graph finds a new version on startup, an **Update** pill appears in the title bar next to Settings, and a notice stays in the corner until you answer it: **Update**, **Release notes**, **Remind me later**, or **Don't check for updates** (you can turn the startup check back on in About).
- Updating opens the installer in Terminal: it downloads the release, checks its checksum and signature, may ask for your administrator password, then quits Git Graph and opens the new version.

### One place for notices

- Results of git actions, CI runs on your branch, new commits after a fetch and long pushes or pulls all appear in the same stack of notices in the bottom-right corner, on every screen.
- Plain notices hide on their own; notices with buttons stay until you answer them. A repeated notice replaces the old one instead of piling up.
- With **Only while Git Graph is in the background** on, notices that come while the window is in front now show inside the app instead of being dropped.

### Switch repositories from the title bar

- The repository name in the title bar opens a dropdown: filter, the current and recent repositories, **Open repository…** (⌘O), **Clone from GitHub…** and **All repositories** (⇧⌘O). Switching happens in place.

### CI/CD: latest release

- Each repository shows its newest release and whether its build passed, plus how many commits on the default branch are not released yet. A failed release build marks the repository as failing; a draft counts as in progress.
- The side pane has a **Latest release** section with the release build's checks.

### Install

Download the file for your system below, or on macOS use **Update** in the app (Settings → About) from 0.5.0 onwards. The builds are not signed with a paid certificate yet: on macOS right-click the app and choose **Open** the first time (or run `xattr -cr "/Applications/Git Graph.app"`); on Windows choose **More info → Run anyway**. Pull requests, Actions and CI/CD use the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) sign-in (`gh auth login`).
